title: 1972 BMW 2002
subtitle: Gloss Black
summary: Round tails, riveted flares, a raw splitter and wide mesh wheels.
thesis: The small sedan that taught America what a sports sedan could be. Light, simple, rear wheel drive, with a parts world that never went away. This one keeps the round taillights, adds riveted flares, a raw aluminum splitter and a cage, and sits on wide mesh wheels.

detailing.note: Wash, then clay. Fifty year old single stage paint holds grime the mitt leaves behind.
Black single stage paint shows every swirl. A gentle polish brings back the depth. Expect black on the pad; that is the paint, and it is normal.
Spray on, wipe off. Ten minutes for months of gloss and water beading.

deck: Lower and wider without losing the shape BMW drew. A Breitspur concept for the car that taught America what a sports sedan could be, and the real parts list to build it.

article.label: The car
article.heading: Why the 2002
body: In 1968 BMW dropped its two liter M10 into the little 1600 two door, partly because its US importer, Max Hoffman, wanted more power. The result weighed about 2,200 pounds, seated four adults and drove like nothing else in its price bracket. It is a big part of why BMW means what it means in America.

Fifty years on, the 2002 is still one of the easiest classics to live with and to build. The mechanicals are simple, the community is deep, and specialists like Ireland Engineering have spent decades making parts for it. That is exactly what you want in a first real project.
article.caption: Side profile. The shape is untouched; everything sits lower and wider.

article.label: The idea
article.heading: Keep the round tails
body: Early cars wear round taillights. BMW switched to square lights for the 1974 model year, and to a lot of owners the car lost a little of its simplicity in the process. This concept keeps the rounds and builds everything else around one rule: lower and wider without losing the shape BMW drew.

That rule rules things out as much as it rules them in. No wing, no body kit, no swap to a modern face. Period flares, mesh wheels, a raw aluminum splitter and a cage, because this car wants a track day.

article.label: The stance
article.heading: Low, then wide, then filled
body: The look comes from three parts working together, and the order matters. Coilovers first, so you can set the ride height and corner weights. Then the flares, because the flares decide how much wheel you can run. Wheels last, once you can measure the real space under the arch.

We spec a 15 by 7 inch mesh wheel at ET25 on the 4 by 100 bolt pattern the 2002 already uses. It fills a Turbo style flare without hanging out of it. Go wider and you are into cutting metal, which is a different project.
article.caption: Raw aluminum splitter, riveted flare and the mesh wheel up close.

article.label: The details
article.heading: The parts you notice second
body: The black grilles change the face more than any other single part. The splitter is a flat aluminum blade under a simple polyethylene air dam, the kind of thing a weekend with a jigsaw and a drill can produce. Out back, a twin outlet Supersprint muffler gives the M10 a proper voice, and the cage turns the cabin into a statement through every window.
article.caption: Round tails stay. Twin tips, tow strap, cage through the glass.

article.label: The cabin
article.heading: Period inside, ready for a track day
body: Inside, the same rule applies. The dash and gauges stay where BMW put them, and the changes are the ones you touch: a small three spoke wheel, a metal ball shift knob, drilled aluminum pedals and black leather sport seats with perforated centers.
The teal door cards are the one hit of color in an all black car, and the cage bars run right past the seats, so you see them every time you open the door.
article.caption: Three spoke wheel, metal shift knob, sport seats and the cage behind them.

article.label: Before you buy
article.heading: What we would tell a friend
body: Black grilles from the 1974 cars bolt to the later nose panel. On a true early car you either fit a later nose or keep the chrome grilles, so check what your car has before ordering. The flares need the arch lip trimmed. The cage listed here comes from Europe and runs about nine weeks, so order it first.
